issues.existing: in a misty moonlit garden by water
issues.observed: the scene is painted in an extremely high-key near-white palette with broad, non-directional ambient brightness and a bright specular streak on the water — it reads visually as bright daylight, yet a crescent moon (upper right) and a lit lantern (on the ground, right edge) are both plainly present in frame
issues.evidence: I recorded the light as genuinely ambiguous rather than clearly nocturnal; 'moonlit' asserts night, which the luminance of the image does not support on its own, but the moon and lit lantern mean I cannot call it daylight either. Flagging rather than correcting.

issues.existing: small seedling with exposed bare roots on the ground
issues.observed: I recorded a small seedling with a few thin leaves rising out of the bare soil, surrounded by dry fallen leaves and thin radiating strands at its base. Whether those strands are exposed roots lying on top of the soil (uprooted) or fine stems/debris around a plant that is still rooted in place cannot be resolved at this tonality.
issues.evidence: The image is near-black in that region; the planted-vs-uprooted distinction is load-bearing but not resolvable. The existing text also asserts it in the scene line ('a small uprooted seedling'). Flagging, not correcting.

issues.existing: nine upright swords displayed one per panel
issues.observed: All nine blades hang POINT-DOWN. In every one of the nine compartments the cruciform hilt and pommel sit at the TOP of the panel and the blade tapers downward to a point at the bottom. None points up.
issues.evidence: Re-opened the image to confirm: top row, middle row and bottom row all show the same arrangement — hilt uppermost, tip lowermost. 'Upright' reads as point-up and misstates the orientation.

issues.existing: a nine-panel wall cabinet holding nine upright swords stands to the left
issues.observed: Same issue in the scene line — the nine blades hang point-down in a 3x3 grid.

issues.existing: the hour of night and the sleepless interior
issues.observed: The window is the scene's only light source and it is filled with a pale, bright overcast sky; it throws hard-edged angled light bands across the stone floor toward the lower left. This is daylight, not night.
issues.evidence: Visible cast shadow streaks on the floor require a strong exterior source; the sky beyond the city skyline is the brightest value in the frame. The room is dark only because it is unlit and heavily curtained.

issues.existing: barefoot figure in a night interior
issues.observed: The figure is barefoot, but the interior is lit by pale daylight through the window, not by night.
